scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8058: Hi IT!! The other floor has STOPPED EXISTING for us
downstairs -- from my computer, every one of them times out, while my own
floor is totally fine!! Something around the big switch that joins the floors
must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at it and reconnect
me to the other floor -- deadlines!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. mswitch0 owns the L3 SVIs for VLAN 10/20/30
  (172.16.10.254 / 172.16.20.254 / 172.16.30.254) and routes between them; a
  VLAN 10 host reaches a VLAN 30 host with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an SVI / inter-VLAN
  fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- VLAN 10 cannot reach
VLAN 30 within Campus 1 -- is NOT reproducible: mswitch0's SVIs (172.16.10.254,
172.16.30.254) are up, and a VLAN 10 host (PC5) reaches a VLAN 30 host
(172.16.30.x) with 0% loss via mswitch0.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-VLAN routing on mswitch0 is
healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the
VLAN10->VLAN30 path, finds it working, checks the SVIs on mswitch0, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a down/misconfigured SVI to satisfy the ticket is
over-diagnosing.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes mswitch0's VLAN 10/30 SVIs are up and inter-VLAN routing works at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
I could not reproduce a cross-floor outage. End-to-end tests show normal inter-floor reachability: from a VLAN 5 workstation (pc1, 10.5.0.1) I successfully pinged multiple hosts on the “other floors” (VLAN 10/20/30: pc5/pc7 172.16.10.x, pc9–pc11 172.16.20.x, pc12–pc14 172.16.30.x) with 0% loss. A topology-wide reachability sweep also shows clean connectivity across all segments. The aggregation switch suspected by the user (mswitch0) has all uplinks (eth2–eth5) up at 10G/full with link detected, and there is no indication of a trunk or interface fault.

Mechanism: If the user experienced timeouts, they were likely due to a local endpoint issue (e.g., stale ARP/DNS cache, host firewall blocking ICMP, or temporary misaddressing) rather than an infrastructure problem. Because VLANs are routed, any inter-floor reachability problem would have shown up broadly; it did not.

Localization: Infrastructure paths between access switches (switch1–3) and the aggregation switch (mswitch0) are healthy. The only plausible locus is the user’s workstation or its immediate port.

Root cause: Not reproducible; most consistent with a transient client-side condition (ARP/DNS cache or host firewall), not a switch or trunk failure.

Corrective fix: Have the affected user flush/renew (ipconfig /flushdns and /renew or equivalent), clear ARP (arp -d -a), verify correct IP/gateway, and ensure ICMP isn’t blocked. If it recurs, capture packets on the user port and check the default gateway reachability at the time of issue. No changes to switches are required.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes mswitch0's VLAN 10/30 SVIs are up and inter-VLAN routing works at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report confirms inter-VLAN reachability but does not explicitly state that mswitch0's VLAN 10 and 30 SVIs are up (addresses/administrative state), so it fails to note the required baseline SVI status.

The agent's tests (multiple successful cross-VLAN pings, mswitch0 link and VLAN outputs, bridge VLAN listing) support the conclusion that inter-VLAN routing is working and the issue is not reproducible. Minor unshown detail (explicit 10G/full speeds) is present in the writeup but overall the investigation justifies the negative diagnosis.
